rail_guard.text: {greeting} Leeds Station. One of the busiest in the North, and we've the queues to prove it.
All aboard for wherever you've been before. Mind the gap and the pigeon.

leeds_lions.text: Shh. It's nearly midnight. They say when the Town Hall clock strikes twelve, the lions get up and go for a walk.
I've waited three nights now. I did see one blink. Or I blinked. One of us blinked.

then.text: Now that's a proper flat cap. You're nearly one of us.

leeds_loiner.text: {greeting} A Loiner, that's what you call someone from Leeds. Nobody's sure why. Something about loins, or loaning, or loitering. I'm loitering, so it fits.
Leeds got rich on wool. Cloth halls, mills, merchants. Then tailoring: at one time Burton's in Leeds was the biggest clothing factory in the world.

leeds_cricket.text: {greeting} Yorkshire cricket. We take it seriously. We take tea seriously too, and that's half a cricket match, tea.
Rugby league's next door. Same ground, different shaped ball, more mud.

leeds_rhubarb.text: {greeting} Forced rhubarb, fresh from the sheds. We grow it in the dark and pick it by candlelight. If you stand still in the shed you can hear it creak as it grows.
It's got protected status now, like champagne. Yorkshire forced rhubarb. Say it with respect.

leeds_temple.text: {greeting} Temple Works. A flax mill dressed up as an Egyptian temple. Daft, beautiful, and they kept sheep on the roof.
Proper sheep. Grass roof. The idea was the turf kept the air damp for the linen thread. And the sheep kept the turf down. Everyone wins, especially the sheep.

leeds_prince.text: This is where it all started, you know. Louis Le Prince stood in a window up there in 1888 and filmed carts going over Leeds Bridge.
Before the famous names in Paris and America. Then he vanished off a train in France in 1890. Biggest mystery in cinema.

leeds_student.text: {greeting} Otley Run tonight. Fancy dress, a pub crawl up the Otley Road, and a lot of people dressed as bananas.
I've an essay due on the Brontës. I'm going to Haworth to soak up the atmosphere. Also the pub.

leeds_utd_fan.text: {greeting} Marching on Together! That's our song. Leeds United, Elland Road, through thick and thin. Mostly thin.
We won the league in 1969, 1974 and 1992. I could tell you about every goal. Pull up a bench.
